design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER, task 1 of title_and_registration (M=2, final task).

STEP 0 DRAW (scripts/draw_counts.py <diff> --task 1): {"task": 1, "key": "env_0041_online_used_car_retailer/title_and_registration/1", "prerequisite_problems": 3, "problems": 4, "factor_counts": [4, 5, 4, 5]}. Assignment: title_ext_late_penalty_payment 4, title_ext_lien_correction_charges 4, title_ext_resubmission_remittance 5, title_ext_late_penalty_reimbursement (root) 5.

SCOPE SNAPSHOT: occupied by task 0: title_ext_shortage_cure_share (pay_title_fee_shortage_f6fcb150; a fee-shortage return that STATES an amount) and title_ext_extension_tag_validity (issue_title_extension_tag_53dbe274). Claimed here: the penalty the state names WITHOUT an amount (pay_title_late_penalty_3594d5af), the lien charges after a lien information error (pay_title_lien_charges_e09cfc3d), the resubmission with remittance (resubmit_title_packet_8a13d7a9) and the late-penalty reimbursement (reimburse_title_late_penalty_e7fb1913). The fee-shortage payments are partitioned by the return itself: a stated amount belongs to the cure share (task 0), a 0.00 return naming a penalty belongs to the penalty payment (task 1). No policy or tool remains unclaimed; this closes the difficulty.

WHY A GOOD TEST: the caller only asks Kestrel to reimburse a late penalty. The reimbursement rule says it is not fixed until the penalty stands collected and is booked only after a remittance follows the return; the resubmission rule says the packet does not go back until the penalty stands collected and only after the lien charges stand collected. The ledger shows two 2026-10-01 returns (lien information error; fee shortage 0.00, notice PN-461873), no collection after them and no remittance after them. The agent must therefore discover three prerequisite problems, compute four numbers over the title ledger, the purchase order and ledger, and the delivery appointment, hand two payments to the buyer, resubmit, and only then reimburse a share that depends on the resubmission itself.

DESIGN THESIS: 'reimburse my late penalty' -> penalty must stand collected (state form) and a remittance must follow the return (state form) -> resubmission waits on the penalty and the lien charges (state form, two sentences) -> penalty 62.90 and lien charges 37.50 paid by the buyer -> remittance 149.40 -> reimbursement 59.83. Depth 3 (lien charges -> resubmission -> reimbursement); breadth: dealer deadline and filing date, lender posting and lien notation, buyer-missed delivery, tag lapse and extension limits, state turnaround, program, document timing.

PROBLEM-TREE CARD: root title_ext_late_penalty_reimbursement. Edges (all value_input, all state form): (1) reimbursement <- penalty payment, gate penalty_paid, sentence 'The late-penalty reimbursement is not fixed until the late-registration penalty named on the order's most recent fee-shortage return stands collected on the order as its own fee entry.' (negated direction: a release waits until what it rests on stands); (2) reimbursement <- resubmission, gate remitted_since, sentence 'The late-penalty reimbursement is booked only after the order's ledger shows a remittance to the state dated on or after its most recent fee-shortage return.' (affirmative); (3) resubmission <- penalty payment, gate held_fees, 'A returned packet does not go back to the state until the late-registration penalty named on a fee-shortage return that states no amount stands collected on the order as its own fee entry.' (negated); (4) resubmission <- lien charges, gate held_fees, 'A packet returned for a lien information error goes back to the state only after the lien charges for the corrected lien stand collected on the order as a lien recording fee entry.' (affirmative). Four-point test each: ordering connective (not until / only after), record-visible state (a collected entry not a schedule fee after the return; a remittance dated after the return; a lien recording fee entry), no tool/id/code token, scope equal to the condition. Uniqueness of the bringing write: only the penalty payment books a collected entry that is not a schedule fee; only the lien-charges payment books a lien recording fee after opening; only the resubmission books a remittance after a return. Unmet at opening: 1a0466d6-0ba9-4273-8ccb-38f636402f01 fee_shortage 0.00 on 2026-10-01 with collections only on 2026-07-06; remittances eb8dd439-d145-4212-be5d-a66e0ae3a22f/d3795bb1-73bc-495e-8329-a3e124bf83f1 on 2026-08-21; aa322689-4008-4a99-a596-8f5c9f2bb1c9 lien_information_error 2026-10-01 after submitted_date 2026-08-21 with the only lien recording fee entry dated 2026-07-06 (collected at opening and remitted 2026-08-21). Owners: both payments are the buyer's (user tools), the resubmission and the reimbursement are Kestrel's (agent tools). Topological order: penalty, lien charges (commute), resubmission, reimbursement. Deletion sensitivity (run): skip penalty -> reimbursement 0.00, remittance 86.50; skip lien charges -> remittance 111.90; skip resubmission -> reimbursement 0.00.

BASE-INVARIANT CARD: payments (title_state_fee_collected): title_service_fees.collect_state (status rejected; 2026-10-01 + 7 collection days = 2026-10-08 >= 2026-10-06) - the fee-shortage clauses of title_service_fees and title_rejections are superseded by the penalty payment's declared overwrites, and the title_rejections clause 'lien_information_error is cured by Kestrel from the finance records' by the lien policy's overwrite (Kestrel corrects the lien data; the buyer pays the state's lien charges for the corrected lien); the opening lien-fee clause is in force and was applied (21.50 collected 2026-07-06 for the outside lender); title_agg_household_fees per-order. Resubmission: title_submission.funded_and_insured (purchase order balance 0.00, insurance_verified true), remit_state (status submitted, set by the same action), title_rejections policy scope (cures in hand -> resubmission within 3 business days); its own-entry remittance clause is superseded (one entry for the total). Reimbursement: title_reimbursements.reimburse_state (status submitted after step 13; rejected already qualifies), one_per_document (notice PN-461873 has no reimbursement on the order); inherited conditions: In-State New Registration reimburses late penalties, the first submission 2026-08-21 missed the NC deadline 2026-08-03, all documents by 2026-07-14 within the 10 due days; the 'in full' clause is superseded by the reimbursed share, and the rule's standard sentence now speaks of the reimbursable penalty, not 'in full'. The resubmission is made ready again and submitted in one action (base lifecycle rejected -> ready_to_submit -> submitted). No time-kind eligibility gate applies to these subjects (temporal_feasibility is empty).

BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD: title order c753d87b-5927-49d4-903c-31d86fac709d of customer ce4265c4-04ef-480c-903e-ea98e6ab2312 on purchase order fc5b5258-7589-4ff3-a7de-2268ce517e17. Penalty object: the fee-shortage return 1a0466d6-0ba9-4273-8ccb-38f636402f01 (notice PN-461873); the reimbursement carries that notice number. Lien object: return aa322689-4008-4a99-a596-8f5c9f2bb1c9; the lienholder field outside_lender, the opening lien recording fee and the credit-union posting f642ab5c-8613-4f45-9b93-4c34821f0fd8 (2026-07-14). Handover object: delivery appointment cd7b5417-001d-4cca-908c-e6e1b9080215 (first slot 2026-07-15 missed by the buyer, delivered 2026-07-29). Remittances 2026-08-21 settle the opening fees by source_txn_id; the new remittance carries the held cures. The opening fees are excluded from the penalty paid (fee_type title_fee/registration_fee) and the penalty entry is excluded from the penalty fee base (fee_type not_applicable).

FACTOR CARD (penalty payment, 4): filing-date rule (method) lien return after the most recent submission -> filed on the collection day 2026-10-06 (baseline remittance date -> 43.95); rate band (parameter) 64 days late -> 0.40 (baseline 0.12 -> 36.37); lien notation (parameter, multi-source: lienholder AND lien return) -> 15.00 (baseline 47.90); return notice (parameter) two returns -> 10.00 (baseline 52.90). Whole baseline 11.37. Near-miss: the 2026-08-21 remittance looks like the filing date, but the lien return voids it.

FACTOR CARD (lien charges, 4; round 4): lien wait clock (method) an outside lender's proceeds were posted -> wait from the most recent submission date 2026-08-21 (other tiers: Kestrel Auto Finance only -> from the lien return date; no lender proceeds -> opening date; all reachable under the purchase charter); baseline opening -> 42.50. Late lien surcharge (parameter) 46 days -> 5.00 (baseline 32.50). Electronic lien filing charge (parameter, cross-difficulty purchase) outside lender 3.00 (baseline 34.50). Lien notation correction charge (parameter, multi-source) a lien recording fee already collected (opening, 21.50) -> 8.00 (baseline 29.50). Whole baseline 21.50. Gold 37.50.

FACTOR CARD (resubmission, 5; round 4): tag lapse clock (method, multi-source) one extension used of min(2, NC 1) and tag expired 2026-09-20 -> lapse from 2026-09-20, 16 days (baseline none -> 124.40); expedite (parameter) > 14 days -> 25.00 (baseline 124.40); channel (parameter, multi-source) electronic with a lien recording fee collected -> 4.00 (baseline 145.40); courier (parameter, cross-difficulty purchase, multi-source) outside lender and lien return -> 12.00 (baseline 137.40); state re-review (parameter) 41-day turnaround -> 8.00 (baseline 141.40). Kestrel's own cost of a stated shortage 0.00 (return states 0.00). Whole baseline 100.40 (held fees). Gold 149.40.

FACTOR CARD (reimbursement, 5; round 4): allocation (method, cross-difficulty purchase, reads the delivery appointment) the buyer missed the first delivery 2026-07-15 and the first submission 2026-08-21 came after the 2026-07-29 handover -> share (64 - 14)/64 = 0.78125 (baseline whole -> 62.90); the other tiers (correction days after a customer-document return; whole penalty) are reachable; end rule (method) lien return then resubmitted -> end 2026-10-06, 64 days (baseline first submission, 18 days, share 4/18 -> 24.67); long wait (parameter) 46 days -> 0.10 (baseline 53.54); program (parameter, cross-difficulty purchase) Certified Plus -> 0.05 (baseline 56.69); prompt documents (parameter) 8 days -> 0.02 (baseline 58.58). Whole baseline 62.90. Gold 59.83. Near-miss: a careless reader counts all 64 late days against Kestrel (62.90); the 14 days the buyer's missed delivery pushed the handover are the buyer's.

SEED ROWS (round 4, checked against blueprint/products/purchase.yaml and delivery.yaml): customer; purchase order (Certified Plus, outside_lender, reserved 2026-07-01 with the 500.00 deposit by credit card, hold to 2026-07-06 = 5 hold days, signed 2026-07-06, handover 2026-07-29, sale final 2026-08-06, balance 0.00, insurance verified); seven purchase ledger rows: deposit, deposit applied at signing, price 26,850.00, NC documentation fee 699.00, sales tax 805.50, ACH down payment 2,000.00 (at least 3 business days before the first dispatch), outside lender proceeds 25,854.50 on 2026-07-14 (8 days after signing, within the 10 funding days, while contracted, before the first dispatch); 28,354.50 - 500.00 - 2,000.00 - 25,854.50 = 0.00. Delivery appointment (Local Home Delivery, 18 miles, booked for Wednesday 2026-07-15, missed with nobody home, missed-appointment fee 99.00 billed 2026-07-15 and paid 2026-07-29, rebooked for Wednesday 2026-07-29 within the 14-day horizon and at least 2 days after the miss, reschedule_count 0, condition report at handover). Title order (rejected, outside_lender, tag NC-T452906 expired 2026-09-20, one extension, submitted 2026-08-21, held 0.00) and 14 title ledger rows: 3 opening fees (title, registration, lien recording 21.50), 4 documents, 2 tags (2026-07-29 -> 2026-08-28; 2026-08-21 -> 2026-09-20), 3 remittances 2026-08-21, 2 returns 2026-10-01.

PERSONA: Theo Rasmussen, clipped and irritated, volunteers the goal (reimburse the late penalty), the notice he received, that his documents went back within the ten days Kestrel gave him (last one day 8) and that the tag ran out on September 20 (all supported by the ledger). Identity and the notice number only when asked. Passive: agrees to pay the penalty when told it must be paid first and pays exactly the stated amount when handed over; same for the lien charges; asks once if the reimbursement is less than the penalty; ends when told the reimbursement was paid. He raises no other payment, filing or tag.

REACHABILITY: every input comes from the six finder reads (title order, title ledger, purchase order, purchase ledger, delivery appointment, delivery ledger); payment amounts are stated by the agent; the buyer's calls return receipts; the resubmission returns a receipt and submitted date; one frozen_time 2026-10-06 14:05 EDT; no external wait.

STANDARD SOLUTION: locate -> verify -> read title order, title ledger, purchase order, purchase ledger, delivery appointment and its ledger -> read the reimbursement policy and its two prerequisite sentences, then the resubmission policy and its two -> compute the penalty 62.90, hand it over -> compute the lien charges 37.50, hand it over -> compute the remittance 149.40 on held 100.40, resubmit -> compute the reimbursement 59.83 on the resubmitted ledger, pay it against PN-461873.

VERIFICATION RUN (round 4; runnable entry: .venv/bin/python skills/erl-task-instantiate/scripts/check_compute.py <diff> --task 1): COMPUTE OK; recomputed 62.90 / 37.50 / 149.40 / 59.83 at handling time with the baselines in factor_sensitivity; the two payments commute (penalty first or lien first give the same figures). Other per-task gates OK (EXTENDED, TASK TOOL CONTRACT, REPLAY with 16 actions, SOLVABILITY, GROUNDING, SCOPE).

CLOSURE: penalty -> pay_title_late_penalty_3594d5af -> step 9 amount 62.90; lien -> pay_title_lien_charges_e09cfc3d -> step 11 amount 37.50; resubmission -> resubmit_title_packet_8a13d7a9 -> step 13 remit_amount 149.40; reimbursement -> reimburse_title_late_penalty_e7fb1913 -> step 15 amount 59.83. Write order 9, 11, 13, 15 is a topological order of the tree. Difficulty-level union: tasks 0 and 1 cover all six extended policies and all six task tools, pairwise disjoint.

DRAFT RECOMPUTATION FROM VISIBLE CONTEXT: with compute/expected masked, the published prose of the four policies, the docstrings, the finder returns and the persona lead to the same four writes in the same order and the same values; the judgement points (the return stating 0.00, the lien return after the last submission, the posting date after the deadline, the tag limit reached) are record values.

REVISIONS: (1) the lien-charges rule gained the sentence 'This applies while the state's return for a lien information error is dated on or after the order's most recent submission.' so that a lien return already cured by resubmission (task 0's 2026-09-09 return) owes nothing; propagated to the factor ladder wording; gates re-run green.

ROUND 2 (audit audits/policy_task/title_and_registration, items for task 1 and charter): T1-F1 / G-F2 (RED): lien_wait_clock no longer conjoins 'a lien information error return stands' (scope); its tiers now turn on whether the order has a remittance and when the outside lender posted, with a reachable fall-through; electronic_lien_filing_charge no longer conjoins the electronic-title-state list (all eight footprint states are in it); lien_renotation_charge (unreachable fall-through) was replaced by lien_notation_correction_charge (a lien fee already collected / none collected but a lienholder recorded / no lienholder). All three keep their tier on this world, so 33.50 and every baseline figure are unchanged. T1-F1 / G-F3 (RED): packet_channel_charge no longer conjoins 'returned at least once'; tiers are mail (reachable for the out-of-state services) / electronic with a lien recording fee collected / electronic without; 4.00 here, remittance unchanged 145.40; the skipped-lien-charges figure moves from 111.90 to 107.90 (channel falls to 0) and edge_load_bearing was updated. G-R1: the resubmission now carries Kestrel's top-up for a stated shortage (0.00 here). G-O1: the lien policy's overwrite now names base title_rejections 'lien_information_error is cured by Kestrel from the finance records' instead of the opening lien clause (G-O3); the penalty policy also declares title_rejections 'fee_shortage by collecting the stated shortage'. G-O2: the penalty overwrite's replacement is self-contained ('after a fee-shortage return that states no amount'). G-O5/T1-O4: the reimbursement rule's standard sentence no longer says 'in full'. G-O7: resubmission tool docstring and rule say ready-and-submitted in one action. G-O9: lien baseline.params lists all eight state keys. T1-O3: persona now says the paperwork went back within the ten days Kestrel gave him (last document on day 8). T1-O2 (submission-count measure): unchanged, recorded only - the order has one submission transition (2026-08-21), so the measure is 1 and below the service's 3; the resubmission makes it 2. T1-O1: covered by the G-O1 declarations. Re-run: all per-task gates OK; the four scored values are unchanged (62.90 / 33.50 / 145.40 / 62.78).

ROUND 3 (audit revision_2 items): G2-R1 (charter RED): the resubmission's Kestrel-funded amount now uses the cure-share policy's own definition, 'the rest of the stated shortage' = stated shortage less the buyer's cure share collected for it as a registration-fee entry on or after that return, and only when no remittance has been made since that return. It no longer subtracts all held fees and cannot pay an already remitted shortage again. Checked: task 0's world after the cure gives 21.95 (44.80 - 22.85); the same world with 33.50 lien charges also held still gives 21.95 (remittance 98.30); on this world the return states 0.00, so 0.00 and 145.40 is unchanged. G2-F1 / T1-F1 (RED): lien_wait_clock no longer conjoins 'the order has a remittance'. Its tiers are anchored on the order's most recent submission date (the packet that went without the lien): lender posted on or before it -> that date; posted after it -> the posting date; no outside lender's proceeds -> the opening date. Every tier divides customers inside the policy's scope. Values unchanged (wait from 2026-08-21, 46 days, 33.50; baseline 38.50). The remittance count and date bindings were removed from the lien computation. G2-O1: the two shared base clauses (title_service_fees shortage clause, title_rejections 'fee_shortage by collecting the stated shortage') are now superseded by one identical sentence carried verbatim in both payment policies: 'Within the service's fee shortage collection days after a fee-shortage return, the buyer pays, as its own entry, either the buyer's cure share of the stated shortage when the return states an amount or the late-registration penalty when the return states no amount; the rest of a stated shortage is Kestrel's own cost.' One replacement, two domains named in it. G2-O2: 'Kestrel still corrects the lien data from the finance records' is no longer a separate restating sentence; the lien policy's first (baseline) sentence and its overwrite replacement now read 'Kestrel corrects the lien data from the finance records and the buyer pays the lien charges ...', which is the very clause the base sentence is replaced by. G2-O3 / T1-O5 (no seed change): the title order opened on 2026-07-06 as a cash purchase with no lienholder to record, so no lien recording fee was due at opening under the restored base clause. The buyer then arranged the credit-union loan, which funded on 2026-08-14 (purchase ledger), and the lienholder became outside_lender. Kestrel's 2026-08-21 packet omitted that lien. That is the lien information error, and it is why the notation is 'added late' (4.00). T1-O2 unchanged (recorded only). Re-run: all per-task and full-suite gates OK; 62.90 / 33.50 / 145.40 / 62.78 unchanged.

ROUND 4 (audit revision_3): G3-F3 / T1-F2 (RED, seed): the outside-lender posting was dated 2026-08-14, 39 days after signing, after handover and closure. Change: re-seeded under the purchase and delivery charters. Hold to reservation + 5; sales tax charge added at signing; lender proceeds 25,854.50 on 2026-07-14; a Local Home Delivery appointment whose 2026-07-15 slot the buyer missed (99.00 fee, paid) and which completed 2026-07-29; handover 2026-07-29 and sale final 2026-08-06; tags at handover; the opening lien recording fee 21.50 collected and remitted as the base clause requires for a lienholder order, which also closes G2-O3 / T1-O5. Persona: delivered at home, credit union paid about a week after signing, missed first delivery on July 15, tag ran out September 20. G3-F1 / T1-F2 (RED, charter): the reimbursed-share ladder's lender tiers could never be reached (outside funding always precedes the dealer deadline). It now allocates against the buyer's own delays the base charter makes possible: the buyer-missed handover (14 days here) or the correction time after a customer-document return; otherwise the whole penalty. Reimbursement 62.78 -> 59.83. G3-F2 / T1-F1 (RED, charter): lien_wait_clock's 'posted after the most recent submission' tier was unreachable; tiers are now outside lender (from the most recent submission date) / Kestrel Auto Finance only (from the lien return date) / no lender proceeds (opening date), all reachable; the clock keeps its tier here. The lien charges rise to 37.50 because the notation-correction tier now sees the opening lien fee (8.00). The remittance becomes 149.40. Two delivery reads were added (steps 6 and 7), shifting the writes to steps 9, 11, 13 and 15. Skipped-edge figures are now 0.00 / 86.50 / 0.00 / 111.90. T1-O2 is unchanged and only recorded.
user_scenario:
You are Theo Rasmussen, 41, a quality engineer in Raleigh, North Carolina. In early July you bought a 2022 Hyundai Tucson SEL from Kestrel Auto, financed mostly through your credit union, and had it delivered to your home. A few days ago the state sent you a notice saying your registration had been returned and that a late-registration penalty is due because the title paperwork went in late. You sent back all of your own paperwork within the ten days Kestrel gave you, so you are convinced the lateness is on Kestrel's side, and you are calling to ask Kestrel to reimburse that late penalty. You are polite but clipped and a little irritated: your temporary tag ran out on September 20 and the car has mostly sat in your driveway since. You want the reimbursement handled on this call.
You share details only when asked: your mobile number is 9195554731, your date of birth is 1985-09-08, the last four digits of your Social Security number are 4258, your ZIP code is 27612 and your email is theo.rasmussen@icloud.com. If the agent asks for the penalty notice number, you read it off the notice: PN-461873. The notice does not show an amount, and you say so if asked. You have no Kestrel order numbers at hand. If asked about the purchase, you say you signed on July 6, the credit union paid its part about a week later, you were not home for the first delivery on July 15 (you paid the missed-delivery fee), and the car was delivered on July 29. If the agent asks how you would like to pay anything, you say the card on your Kestrel account is fine.
If the agent explains that the penalty itself has to be paid before Kestrel can reimburse anything, you grumble that it seems backwards but agree, and when the agent hands the payment over to you, you make it yourself for exactly the amount the agent told you. If the agent explains that there is also a charge for recording your credit union's lien that has to be paid, you agree to that too and pay it yourself for exactly the amount the agent gives you once it is handed over. You do not raise any other payment, filing or tag yourself, and you never suggest what should be done first.
When the agent tells you how much Kestrel is reimbursing you and that the reimbursement has been paid, you say thanks, that you will watch for it, and end the call. If the agent says the reimbursement is less than the penalty, you ask once why, accept the explanation and end the call.

No other order is entailed.
